change.title: feat(web): record commands in a receipt ledger and sweep unfinished turns at host start
change.description: ## Summary - A retry after a lost reply can run a command twice. Only `send_prompt` has a command id today. - This PR adds a receipt ledger on the host. A resend with the same command id returns the first outcome. The host does not run the command again. - This PR also writes one `interrupted` terminator for every turn that a host crash left open. It runs before any client can connect. - This is the first of four pull requests. The next pull requests add terminals and domain routes, the client command state, and the client facades. Until the last one merges, a request without a command id works as before. ## Related Issue Refs #1068 No open or closed pull request covers this problem. Issue #823 overlaps in part. This PR does not close it. ## Type of Change - [x] feat: new feature - [ ] fix: bug fix - [ ] docs: documentation only - [ ] style: formatting or non-functional styling changes - [ ] refactor: internal cleanup with no behavior change - [ ] perf: performance improvement - [ ] test: adds or updates tests - [ ] build: build or dependency changes - [ ] ci: CI/CD workflow changes - [ ] chore: maintenance or tooling - [ ] revert: reverts a previous change ## What Changed - New command ledger. The host records a command before it runs it. A dropped handler leaves an "unknown" mark. The host never runs that command again. - Outcomes stay for the receipt retention time. Bare ids stay longer. An evicted outcome gives `outcome_unknown`. - A resend finds the entity first. Sessions and agents carry the command id that created them. This works after eviction and after a host restart. - One admission point in the socket request loop, after the capability check. The 14 desktop `acp_*` commands use the same helper. - Replies of session commands carry `visible_at`. The ledger never stores credentials or request bodies. - New error codes: `command_conflict`, `invalid_command_id`, `agent_unavailable`, `invalid_agent_config`. A missing agent binary or a bad agent config is a final rejection. - A completed `send_prompt` turn stays known after a host restart. A resend does not run it again. - The host-start sweeper appends `prompt_complete` with `interrupted` for each open turn. It runs inside session store open. - `--receipt-retention-secs` now takes effect on `termul-server`. ## How It Was Tested - [x] `bun run ci` (Biome lint + format + imports, strict mode) - [x] `bun run typecheck` - [x] `bun run test` - [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` (in src-tauri) - [x] `cargo test` (in src-tauri) - [ ] Manual verification completed - [ ] Not applicable One chat code-block test timed out under load in the full run. It passes alone and this PR does not touch it. Fault tests run through the real relay loop with a fake agent: lost reply and resend, resend in flight, eviction of a create and a non-create, create resend after restart, same id with another request, rejected `send_prompt`, and the sweeper on a crashed log. Both clippy gates pass. ## Screenshots or Recordings No user-visible UI change. This PR changes the host only. The evidence is the test run above. ## CI & Review Gate - [ ] All CI checks pass (PR Validation, Rust Checks, Build Verification, Security Scans) - [ ] Code review comments from CodeRabbit / Claude have been addressed or resolved - [ ] No unresolved review findings remain ## Checklist - [x] My PR title follows the conventional commit format used by this repo - [x] I linked the related issue or explained why none exists - [ ] I updated docs when needed - [x] I added or updated tests when needed - [x] I verified the change does not introduce unrelated modifications - [x] I read AGENTS.md and followed the contributor guidelines - [ ] A human reviewed the complete diff before submission --- ## Summary by cubic Adds a host-side command receipt ledger so a retry of a lost reply never runs the same command twice, and sweeps turns left open by a host crash as `interrupted` at startup. - A resend with the same `commandId` returns the first outcome instead of re-executing. Create commands are resolved from the stamped entity after ledger eviction or a host restart. - Requests without a `commandId` behave exactly as before; `send_prompt` uses its `turnId` as the `commandId`. - Completed turns are restored from durable history after a host restart, so a resend of a completed `turnId` is accepted even before a client subscribes. - Ledgered replies never store credentials, request bodies, or prompt content. Session-scoped replies carry `visible_at`. - Missing agent binaries and invalid agent configs (including blank name/command after trim) now fail fast with `agent_unavailable` and `invalid_agent_config` error codes instead of `unsupported`. - The host-start sweeper appends `prompt_complete` with `interrupted` for every unfinished turn before any client connects. - `--receipt-retention-secs` now takes effect on `termul-server`, clamps to a 7-day maximum, and queues a warning when clamped. - Adds the `set_default_project` WebSocket request type (idempotent, ledgered). This is the first of four PRs; the remaining ones add terminals and domain routes, client command state, and client facades. Written for commit 44e25e5bc733af63cc6ed62b489a274691dff24b. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * WebSocket and desktop commands now support command IDs, allowing repeated requests to replay recorded results and report conflicts when an ID is reused for a different request. * Completed turn history is restored after restart, and sessions with interrupted turns are marked accordingly. * Added WebSocket support for `unwatch_project` and `set_default_project`. * **Bug Fixes** * Agent launch errors now distinguish unavailable agents from invalid configurations. * Agent configuration names and commands are trimmed, and blank values are rejected with clearer errors.

+//! Typed prefixes for deterministic agent-spawn failures (AD-5).
+//!
+//! A missing agent binary or an invalid agent config is a definite rejection:
+//! retrying the same request cannot succeed, so clients must never retry it
+//! automatically. The manager's `Err(String)` boundary carries the verdict as
+//! a stable prefix (the [`ACP_AUTH_REQUIRED_PREFIX`](super::ACP_AUTH_REQUIRED_PREFIX)
+//! convention) so the WS layer maps it to a `WsErrorCode` and the desktop
+//! renderer prefix-matches the same string.
+
+/// The agent binary is missing, not installed, or the process cannot start.
+pub const ACP_AGENT_UNAVAILABLE: &str = "ACP_AGENT_UNAVAILABLE";
+
+/// The agent config is unusable (empty name, command or `configId`).
+pub const ACP_INVALID_AGENT_CONFIG: &str = "ACP_INVALID_AGENT_CONFIG";
+
+/// Which deterministic spawn failure a tagged error string carries.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub enum SpawnFailure {
+    AgentUnavailable,
+    InvalidAgentConfig,
+}
+
+/// Tag `detail` as [`SpawnFailure::AgentUnavailable`].
+pub(crate) fn agent_unavailable(detail: impl std::fmt::Display) -> String {
+    format!("{ACP_AGENT_UNAVAILABLE}: {detail}")
+}
+
+/// Tag `detail` as [`SpawnFailure::InvalidAgentConfig`].
+pub(crate) fn invalid_agent_config(detail: impl std::fmt::Display) -> String {
+    format!("{ACP_INVALID_AGENT_CONFIG}: {detail}")
+}
+
+/// Split a tagged spawn error into its verdict and the human message.
+/// `None` for any untagged error.
+pub(crate) fn classify_spawn_error(error: &str) -> Option<(SpawnFailure, &str)> {
+    [
+        (ACP_AGENT_UNAVAILABLE, SpawnFailure::AgentUnavailable),
+        (ACP_INVALID_AGENT_CONFIG, SpawnFailure::InvalidAgentConfig),
+    ]
+    .into_iter()
+    .find_map(|(prefix, failure)| {
+        error
+            .strip_prefix(prefix)
+            .and_then(|rest| rest.strip_prefix(": "))
+            .map(|message| (failure, message))
+    })
+}
+
+/// Whether a recorded driver start failure is the OS refusing to launch the
+/// agent program for a deterministic reason: the program or its path is
+/// missing, it is not executable, or it is not a runnable binary.
+///
+/// The SDK hands the driver only the stringified spawn `io::Error`
+/// (`Error::into_internal_error`), so its kind is gone and matching is
+/// wording-based. The needles are the OS error texts Rust prints for the
+/// launch errnos, per platform: Unix `ENOENT` / `EACCES` / `ENOEXEC`
+/// ("No such file or directory", "Permission denied", "Exec format error") and
+/// Windows os errors 2 / 3 / 5 / 193 ("cannot find the file / path specified",
+/// "Access is denied", "is not a valid Win32 application"), plus the `which`-style
+/// "program not found" and the shell's "is not recognized as an internal or
+/// external command". A failure with none of these (a driver panic, a runtime
+/// build failure, a process that died before `initialize`) may be transient and
+/// must stay untagged.
+pub(crate) fn is_launch_refusal(detail: &str) -> bool {
+    const REFUSALS: [&str; 10] = [
+        "no such file or directory",
+        "program not found",
+        "permission denied",
+        "exec format error",
+        "cannot find the file specified",
+        "cannot find the path specified",
+        "access is denied",
+        "is not a valid win32 application",
+        "is not recognized as an internal or external command",
+        "command not found",
+    ];
+    let lower = detail.to_ascii_lowercase();
+    REFUSALS.iter().any(|needle| lower.contains(needle))
+}

+//! The command class table: how every `/ws` request type (and, through the
+//! shared admission helper, every Tauri `acp_*` command) is treated by the
+//! receipt ledger. Mirrored 1:1 by `WS_COMMAND_CLASSES` in
+//! `src/shared/types/web-protocol.types.ts`; `class_tests` pins the parity.
+//!
+//! | kind         | meaning                                                         |
+//! |--------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
+//! | `Create`     | makes a host-minted entity; the `commandId` is stamped on it    |
+//! | `Command`    | mutates state, not naturally idempotent                         |
+//! | `Idempotent` | sets a value or deletes by id; a repeat answers like the first  |
+//! | `Read`       | no mutation                                                     |
+//!
+//! `Create` and `Command` carry a [`Replay`] policy: `Payload` replays the
+//! stored (sanitized) reply, `Entity` rebuilds it from the entity the command
+//! stamped, `ReceiptOnly` never stores a payload (credential-bearing kinds).
+//! `send_prompt` is `Command` + `Entity`: its `turnId` is its `commandId` and
+//! `TurnWatermark` is its entity-lookup layer, so it never enters the ledger.
+
+use serde_json::Value;
+use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
+
+/// What a request type is, for the ledger.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub enum ClassKind {
+    Create,
+    Command,
+    Idempotent,
+    Read,
+}
+
+/// How a settled command is answered on a same-id resend.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub enum Replay {
+    /// The stored, size-bounded reply payload.
+    Payload,
+    /// Rebuilt from the entity that carries the `commandId`.
+    Entity,
+    /// Success only; the payload (it may carry secrets) is never stored.
+    ReceiptOnly,
+}
+
+/// One row of the class table.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub struct CommandClass {
+    pub kind: ClassKind,
+    /// `Some` for `Create` and `Command`.
+    pub replay: Option<Replay>,
+}
+
+impl CommandClass {
+    const fn create() -> Self {
+        Self {
+            kind: ClassKind::Create,
+            replay: Some(Replay::Entity),
+        }
+    }
+    const fn command(replay: Replay) -> Self {
+        Self {
+            kind: ClassKind::Command,
+            replay: Some(replay),
+        }
+    }
+    const fn idempotent() -> Self {
+        Self {
+            kind: ClassKind::Idempotent,
+            replay: None,
+        }
+    }
+    const fn read() -> Self {
+        Self {
+            kind: ClassKind::Read,
+            replay: None,
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Whether a request of this class with a `commandId` enters the ledger.
+    /// `send_prompt` (`Command` + `Entity`) does not: `TurnWatermark` owns it.
+    #[must_use]
+    pub const fn ledgered(self) -> bool {
+        match self.kind {
+            ClassKind::Create => true,
+            ClassKind::Command => !matches!(self.replay, Some(Replay::Entity)),
+            ClassKind::Idempotent | ClassKind::Read => false,
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Whether the entity the command created is looked up on a resend that
+    /// finds no stored outcome.
+    #[must_use]
+    pub const fn creates_entity(self) -> bool {
+        matches!(self.kind, ClassKind::Create)
+    }
+
+    /// Whether the reply payload may be stored for replay.
+    #[must_use]
+    pub const fn stores_payload(self) -> bool {
+        !matches!(self.replay, Some(Replay::ReceiptOnly))
+    }
+}
+
+/// Every `/ws` request type and its class. Tauri `acp_*` commands map onto
+/// these rows by [`tauri_request_type`].
+pub const WS_COMMAND_CLASSES: &[(&str, CommandClass)] = &[
+    ("send_prompt", CommandClass::command(Replay::Entity)),
+    ("cancel_prompt", CommandClass::idempotent()),
+    ("set_config_option", CommandClass::idempotent()),
+    ("set_mode", CommandClass::idempotent()),
+    ("set_model", CommandClass::idempotent()),
+    // One-shot tickets: a duplicate answer is `already_resolved`, so a lost
+    // reply + resend of the same commandId must replay the original outcome.
+    ("respond_permission", CommandClass::command(Replay::Payload)),
+    ("answer_question", CommandClass::command(Replay::Payload)),
+    ("create_session", CommandClass::create()),
+    ("load_session", CommandClass::command(Replay::Payload)),
+    ("resume_session", CommandClass::command(Replay::Payload)),
+    ("close_session", CommandClass::command(Replay::Payload)),
+    (
+        "dispose_ephemeral_session",
+        CommandClass::command(Replay::Payload),
+    ),
+    ("promote_session", CommandClass::command(Replay::Payload)),
+    ("list_sessions", CommandClass::read()),
+    (
+        "register_discovered_session",
+        CommandClass::command(Replay::Payload),
+    ),
+    ("spawn_agent", CommandClass::create()),
+    ("kill_agent", CommandClass::idempotent()),
+    ("list_agents", CommandClass::read()),
+    ("authenticate", CommandClass::read()),
+    (
+        "authenticate_agent",
+        CommandClass::command(Replay::ReceiptOnly),
+    ),
+    ("logout_agent", CommandClass::idempotent()),
+    ("delete_agent_session", CommandClass::idempotent()),
+    (
+        "respond_elicitation",
+        CommandClass::command(Replay::ReceiptOnly),
+    ),
+    ("subscribe", CommandClass::read()),
+    ("ping", CommandClass::read()),
+    ("list_persisted_sessions", CommandClass::read()),
+    ("delete_session", CommandClass::idempotent()),
+    ("open_persisted_session", CommandClass::read()),
+    ("get_session_payload", CommandClass::read()),
+    ("recover_session_snapshot", CommandClass::read()),
+    ("get_session_cursor", CommandClass::read()),
+    ("get_session_payload_tail", CommandClass::read()),
+    ("list_acp_catalog", CommandClass::read()),
+    ("set_catalog_opt_in", CommandClass::idempotent()),
+    ("install_acp_agent", CommandClass::command(Replay::Payload)),
+    (
+        "acp_deliver_auth_redirect",
+        CommandClass::command(Replay::ReceiptOnly),
+    ),
+    ("store_read", CommandClass::read()),
+    ("store_write", CommandClass::idempotent()),
+    ("store_delete", CommandClass::idempotent()),
+    ("add_project", CommandClass::idempotent()),
+    ("update_project", CommandClass::idempotent()),
+    ("remove_project", CommandClass::idempotent()),
+    ("set_default_project", CommandClass::idempotent()),
+    (
+        "record_agent_switch",
+        CommandClass::command(Replay::Payload),
+    ),
+    ("watch_project", CommandClass::read()),
+    ("unwatch_project", CommandClass::read()),
+];
+
+/// The class of a `/ws` request type; `None` for a type the host does not
+/// serve (it answers `not_implemented`).
+#[must_use]
+pub fn class_of(request_type: &str) -> Option<(&'static str, CommandClass)> {
+    #[cfg(test)]
+    if request_type == "panic_for_test" {
+        return Some(("panic_for_test", CommandClass::command(Replay::Payload)));
+    }
+    WS_COMMAND_CLASSES
+        .iter()
+        .find(|(name, _)| *name == request_type)
+        .map(|(name, class)| (*name, *class))
+}
+
+/// The class-table row a Tauri `acp_*` command shares with its `/ws`
+/// request type, for the commands the table covers.
+#[must_use]
+pub fn tauri_request_type(command: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
+    Some(match command {
+        "acp_spawn_agent" => "spawn_agent",
+        "acp_new_session" => "create_session",
+        "acp_load_session" => "load_session",
+        "acp_resume_session" => "resume_session",
+        "acp_close_session" => "close_session",
+        "acp_dispose_ephemeral_session" => "dispose_ephemeral_session",
+        "acp_promote_session" => "promote_session",
+        "acp_register_discovered_session" => "register_discovered_session",
+        "acp_record_agent_switch" => "record_agent_switch",
+        "acp_authenticate" => "authenticate_agent",
+        "acp_logout" => "logout_agent",
+        "acp_auth_deliver_redirect" => "acp_deliver_auth_redirect",
+        "acp_respond_elicitation" => "respond_elicitation",
+        "acp_delete_agent_session" => "delete_agent_session",
+        "acp_install_agent" => "install_acp_agent",
+        _ => return None,
+    })
+}
+
+/// The payload fields that identify WHAT a request of this type acts on:
+/// entity names only (dotted paths reach into objects). Never args, env, text,
+/// urls, tokens or any other content, so a fingerprint derives from nothing
+/// secret and one id is consistent across the `/ws` and Tauri carriers (which
+/// build the same field names).
+fn identifying_fields(request_type: &str) -> &'static [&'static str] {
+    match request_type {
+        "create_session" => &["agentId", "cwd", "projectId"],
+        "spawn_agent" => &["config.name", "config.command", "config.configId"],
+        "load_session" | "resume_session" => &["agentId", "sessionId", "cwd"],
+        "close_session" | "dispose_ephemeral_session" | "promote_session"
+        | "delete_agent_session" => &["agentId", "sessionId"],
+        "register_discovered_session" => &["agentId", "sessionId", "cwd", "projectId"],
+        "record_agent_switch" => &["sessionId", "fromConfigId", "toConfigId", "newSessionId"],
+        "respond_permission" => &["agentId", "requestId", "optionId"],
+        "answer_question" => &["agentId", "questionId"],
+        "authenticate_agent" => &["agentId", "methodId"],
+        "respond_elicitation" => &["agentId", "requestId", "action"],
+        "acp_deliver_auth_redirect" | "install_acp_agent" | "logout_agent" | "kill_agent" => {
+            &["agentId"]
+        }
+        _ => &[],
+    }
+}
+
+/// The scalar (string, number or bool) at a dotted `path` of `payload`, in a
+/// type-tagged form so `1`, `"1"` and `true` stay distinct. `null` and an
+/// absent field are both "absent".
+fn scalar_at(payload: &Value, path: &str) -> Option<String> {
+    let value = path
+        .split('.')
+        .try_fold(payload, |value, key| value.get(key))?;
+    match value {
+        // Trimmed, and blank means absent: the same normalization the
+        // handlers apply to ids (`projectId`), so a request differing only in
+        // padding is the same command.
+        Value::String(text) => {
+            let text = text.trim();
+            (!text.is_empty()).then(|| format!("s{text}"))
+        }
+        Value::Number(number) => Some(format!("n{number}")),
+        Value::Bool(flag) => Some(format!("b{flag}")),
+        _ => None,
+    }
+}
+
+/// A 128-bit digest of the request type and its identifying fields. Two
+/// requests with one `commandId` but different fingerprints are a
+/// `command_conflict`; a request differing only in a non-identifying field
+/// (args, env, text...) is the same command.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub struct Fingerprint([u8; 16]);
+
+impl Fingerprint {
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn of(request_type: &str, payload: &Value) -> Self {
+        let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
+        hasher.update(request_type.as_bytes());
+        hasher.update([0]);
+        for path in identifying_fields(request_type) {
+            if let Some(value) = scalar_at(payload, path) {
+                hasher.update(path.as_bytes());
+                hasher.update([1]);
+                hasher.update(value.len().to_le_bytes());
+                hasher.update(value.as_bytes());
+            }
+        }
+        let digest = hasher.finalize();
+        let mut out = [0u8; 16];
+        out.copy_from_slice(&digest[..16]);
+        Self(out)
+    }
+}

+/**
